scope: Elite Dangerous multiplayer, Teams/Wings, Team Beacon and Nav-Lock, instancing, shared rewards and Team Missions, telepresence and physical multicrew, multicrew roles, Ship-Launched Fighters, on-foot teamwork, squad coordination, and the 2026 Operations system used by the Mongrels Field Manual and Ask the Mongrels.

entries.ruleOfThumb: A normal Elite team supports up to four Commanders. 'Wing' is the older name and is still common community shorthand; Odyssey calls the group a Team.
details: Teams let separate ships coordinate travel, combat, missions and rewards while remaining independent vessels.
A Team is not the same thing as Multicrew: Team members usually fly their own ships, while Multicrew places multiple Commanders aboard one ship or vehicle.
The four-Commander Team limit is important for squad planning; larger groups must coordinate across multiple Teams.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Use the Team Beacon as the dependable rendezvous signal and treat Nav-Lock as a convenience rather than something the operation should depend on.
details: A Team Beacon makes a teammate's normal-space location visible to teammates in supercruise so they can target it and drop into that location.
Nav-Lock is intended to help a follower track a teammate's supercruise and hyperspace transitions when requirements are met.
Nav-Lock has a long history of inconsistent behavior, so experienced groups often use the beacon, direct target selection and voice comms as the reliable fallback.

entries.topic: Instancing and Getting the Team Together
entries.ruleOfThumb: Being in the same Team helps matchmaking but does not guarantee everyone is already in the same local instance. Use a common anchor, Team Beacon and synchronized re-entry before assuming the activity is broken.
details: First verify everyone is in the same game mode and has actually joined the Team.
Have one Commander act as the anchor with Team Beacon on; teammates can return to supercruise and drop on that beacon.
If needed, leave and re-enter the local instance, reform the Team, or have the separated Commander relog before rebuilding the group.
For large squad events, establish the anchor before combat starts so late arrivals have a clear target.

entries.topic: Team Bounties, Trade Dividends and Exploration Sharing
entries.ruleOfThumb: Do not assume every multiplayer activity splits one reward pot. Elite uses activity-specific sharing rules: combat rewards can be duplicated for qualifying teammates, trade escorts can receive a dividend, and exploration sharing depends on team/system participation.
details: Current Team rules award qualifying teammates their own bounty reward when they participate in the same kill rather than dividing one bounty among the group.
A teammate escort can receive a trade dividend equal to 5% of the trader's commodity profit while the trader keeps the normal sale profit.
Exploration discoveries can be shared with teammates under the Team exploration rules when the relevant commanders are together in the system.
Mission rewards follow mission-sharing rules instead of these generic Team reward rules.

entries.ruleOfThumb: The mission owner shares the mission from Transactions and teammates must accept it. Each Commander can share one Team Mission at a time, allowing up to four simultaneously shared Team Missions in a four-person Team.
details: The Commander who accepted the Team Mission is the owner and controls the share.
For cargo Team Missions, the Mission Depot lets the group collect and deliver the required cargo over multiple runs.
Eligible teammates receive their own completion reward rather than splitting the owner's reward.
Do not assume ordinary missions, on-foot shared missions and Team Missions have identical completion/turn-in behavior; read the specific mission state before reorganizing the Team.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Telepresence Multicrew is remote drop-in crew: the guest is projected directly into another Commander's ship rather than physically travelling to it.
details: Telepresence is useful when Commanders are far apart because the guest does not need to fly to the host first.
The host remains the Helm/ship owner and the guest takes an available crew role.
Because the guest is remote rather than physically aboard, telepresence is not the right mode when the plan requires physically disembarking together for Odyssey surface activity.
Telepresence and ordinary Team play are separate multiplayer modes with different limitations.

sources.name: Frontier Forums — Telepresence vs physical boarding discussion

entries.ruleOfThumb: Use physical multicrew when the group needs to travel together in one ship and later disembark together. The guest physically boards the host ship rather than joining by telepresence.
details: Physical multicrew requires the Commanders to meet and board the same compatible ship in Odyssey.
Because the Commanders are physically present, the group can travel and later continue the session on foot instead of being limited to a remote bridge projection.

Physical multicrew and telepresence have historically had different role and interaction quirks, so the assistant should not promise that every telepresence function behaves identically when physically crewed.

entries.topic: Helm, Gunner and Fighter Con Roles
entries.ruleOfThumb: The ship owner is always Helm. Gunner operates supported turreted weapons/utilities, while Fighter Con pilots a Ship-Launched Fighter when the ship has an appropriate fighter hangar.
details: Helm retains primary ship control, navigation and normal piloting responsibilities.
Gunner is built around turreted weapon control and compatible scanner/utility access rather than taking over the ship itself.
Fighter Con launches into an SLF while the mothership remains under Helm control.
Crew can change available roles during a session, but the host remains Helm.

entries.ruleOfThumb: A compatible multicrew ship can support player-controlled SLFs, and multicrew can allow up to two active player-controlled fighters when the fighter bay and crew arrangement support it.
details: SLFs operate locally around the mothership and cannot independently enter supercruise or hyperspace.
Fighter Con is the dedicated multicrew role for a human SLF pilot.
The Mongrels permit SLFs generally but strongly discourage them in PvP because synchronization and lag can degrade the fight for other players.
For organized PvP, follow the squad event rules even if the game mechanically allows the fighter.

entries.ruleOfThumb: For Odyssey surface work, form a Team first and use physical travel when you want to stay together through ship, SRV and on-foot phases. Shared on-foot missions still require each teammate to accept the share.
details: The Scorpion is the standard two-seat SRV and can support a driver plus another crew position.
On-foot missions can be shared to Team members, who individually accept or decline the invitation.
A teammate can assist with combat or objectives even when the mission ownership/reward path remains tied to the mission host.
Use voice comms and assign roles before entering hostile settlements; the game does not automatically coordinate targets or legal consequences for the group.

entries.ruleOfThumb: For Mongrel squad activity, Open Play is the standard. BGS actions intended to affect a faction or system must be performed in Open, and Solo/PG must not be used to avoid opposition.
details: Form Teams, establish voice comms and choose an anchor before beginning an organized squad action.
Open Play is part of the squad's teamwork and accountability standard, not merely a matchmaking preference.
If technical issues force a mode change, that exception does not convert Solo/PG into an acceptable way to perform contested BGS work.

sources.name: Regiment of Imperial Mongrels — Squad Rules

entries.ruleOfThumb: Operations are a separate structured co-op activity introduced in 2026, not a replacement name for ordinary Teams or Team Missions. They support up to four Commanders in multi-stage squad scenarios.
details: Operations can be started by a lone Commander or a formed squad, with optional matchmaking available to fill open positions.
The Operation Runner transports participating Commanders to the scenario and serves as the deployment hub.
The system launched with six Operations, with additional scenarios planned after launch.
Mercenary Mode is the default no-Powerplay-consequence mode; Powerplay Mode lets eligible squads perform Operations with Powerplay strategic effects.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Operations reward each Commander directly. Current reward types include Credits, Materials and Merc Coin, with Merits also available where applicable in Powerplay Mode.
details: Merc Coin is earned through Operations and is spent on the Operations reward ecosystem, including special module/engineering offerings.
Powerplay Mode can award Merits in addition to the normal Operation rewards when the Commander is eligible.
Frontier has already adjusted and fixed Operations reward behavior since launch, so exact payout/meta-farming questions should be live-verified before giving precise numbers.

sources.name: Elite Dangerous — Operations Update follow-up fixes

entries.ruleOfThumb: More than four Commanders requires multiple normal Teams. Use one shared rendezvous/anchor and coordinate the separate Team leaders rather than constantly reshuffling everyone mid-operation.
details: Pick one Commander or one Team as the location anchor and keep a beacon available for arrivals where practical.
Assign Team leaders and keep the groups stable so mission ownership, nav-lock targets and voice coordination remain understandable.
A large group can occupy the same activity area, but separate Teams still retain their own Team-level mission and navigation relationships.
For combat, agree target calls, regroup points and retreat/high-wake directions before contact.

entries.ruleOfThumb: For ordinary squad play: choose the activity and mode first, form the Team, establish voice/text comms, select an anchor, turn on the Team Beacon, share missions deliberately, then move together. Use Multicrew only when multiple Commanders actually need to operate one vessel; use Operations for the dedicated 2026 scenario system.
details: Choose Team play when Commanders need their own ships and independent loadouts.
Choose telepresence Multicrew for instant remote crew access to one vessel; choose physical multicrew when the group needs to travel and disembark together.
Choose Operations when the objective is one of Frontier's structured multi-stage squad scenarios rather than ordinary galaxy activity.
When an instance breaks, regroup before continuing instead of letting half the squad progress objectives in a separate instance.
